A tone that rises with lift; also in the menu\'s Quick settings
The phone\'s media volume applies on top.
Auto plays speed to fly in cruise. It needs an airspeed sensor; without one, it stays on the vario.
Silent while the lift is between the two values below
Short callouts in flight through the phone\'s voice, so your eyes stay outside; the screen may be off.
This phone has no text-to-speech voice: Android\'s settings install one (Text-to-speech output).
Ahead and inside: “Airspace ahead: Grenoble CTR, in 40 seconds”
Above it, and dropped below: “Above final glide by 120 metres”
Start, each turn point and the finish, with the next point
Leaving a climb, its average and the height gained: “Climb 2.1, gained 450”
Above the field when you land there: arrival heights and reach use it.

Your glide cone: a field is in reach only at this glide ratio, with the wind and the terrain, arriving at the arrival height. You are warned when none is left. Final glide and speed to fly keep the glider\'s polar.
Kept between the glide path and the terrain on final glide.
The MacCready of the reach and of the arrival heights at fields.
0 while the safety glide ratio is on.
The MacCready for speed to fly when the app starts; changing it sets the MacCready now too.
Lowers MacCready for speed to fly as you get low: 0 off, 0.3 is common.
How the alternates, the fields in reach, are sorted.
A green triangle on your track: the last point from which the target is still in reach
Used at once, until a newer estimate replaces it.
Estimate the wind while circling. Needs only a GPS.
Estimate the wind in glides. Needs an airspeed sensor.
Take the wind of other instruments.
Drift the snail trail with the wind while circling, at close map scales.
None yet: circle to estimate it, or set it by hand
Airspace ahead, inside, or crossing the task
Off: nothing warns of airspace ahead or inside in flight.

Vibrate for a new warning, and when it gets worse
The banner counts down, then goes; it comes back if the warning gets worse

NOTAMs whose Q-code starts with one of these are hidden (QA: aerodromes, QN: navaids, QOL: obstacle lights…).

Turns true bearings into magnetic ones, as the controller uses.

Pilots, parachutes and baggage: all on board but the glider and the water.
This plane carries no water ballast.

Above the glider\'s maximum take-off mass.
No barometer: Buteo uses the GPS altitude. QNH still converts flight levels for airspace.
Not set yet: Buteo sets it after a while on the ground at an airfield, or set it here. Until then it uses the GPS altitude.
Buteo sets it as you fly; changing it by hand turns this off.
On final glide: the highest MacCready that still gets you home.
The average climb of your recent thermals.
The average climb, then on final glide the highest MacCready that still gets you home.

In XCSoarData/tasks, as a .tsk file XCSoar reads too.
No route files. Saved routes go to XCSoarData/tasks; tasks in SeeYou .cup files there are found too.

The start is when you leave its zone, not when you enter it
Navigate to the nearest point of the start and finish zones.

A replay: nothing was recorded, nothing to share.
The flight log closes a little after the landing; Share and WeGlide follow.
No flight log found: %1$s has the recorded ones.
To upload to WeGlide, set your pilot ID: %1$s.
Replay and Delete: on the ground.
%1$s goes from the phone for good. Copies shared or on WeGlide stay.
Not created: \"%1$s\" is taken or not a file name
Buteo saves %1$s and restarts with the settings of %2$s.
Its settings are lost. Data files, planes and flights stay.
A profile holds Buteo\'s settings: units, map, airspace, safety heights, data files, tiles, the plane. Pilots sharing a phone, or a club, each keep their own. Buteo restarts to switch.
In flight: profiles switch on the ground only.
No weather received: check the internet connection and the codes
Add the airports whose METAR and TAF you want. Buteo downloads them from NOAA (internet needed); the map shows the stations.
Thermals, wind and clouds forecast over the map, from thermalmap.info for many countries. New every day.
The file has no forecast: download today\'s.
Dashed: climb tops in blue, climb bases in grey.
Dashed: climb tops in blue, climb bases in grey. Shaded: terrain.
Climb history: the average of each climb
Each bar is one climb, as wide as it lasted. Dashed: MacCready %1$s and the climb trend.
Needs a route: the chart starts once the route has started.
Dashed: the trend in blue, and the speed the polar gives at the current MacCready (Vest) in grey.
Contest: the flight and the scored path
Thermal band: climb rate by height
Grey: the climbs so far by height; blue: this climb. The dot is your height at your MacCready; dashed red, the MacCready the risk factor allows; grey lines, the working band.
Vario histogram: how often each climb rate was flown
Blue: circling; grey: cruise. Dashed: your MacCready, and the sink at the best glide speed.
Blue: circling; grey: cruise. Dashed: your MacCready.
The line: wind speed by height. Arrows: where it blows, north up.
Needs climbs: Buteo measures the wind while circling.
No polar: choose the plane in %1$s.
Dashed red: the speed to fly in sink and lift at MacCready %1$s; blue: the climb rates flown.
Vopt: the speed to fly between climbs; Vave: the average cross-country speed. Dashed red: your MacCready.
Needs an outside air temperature from a device (a vario or a probe); the phone has none.
Black: air temperature; dashed red: the dry adiabat; dashed blue: dew point.
Route: its points and the flight
